svg.text: From the human-orthodox list to the submitted one: twelve cards, each with a measurement or a reason
Parent = a July 14 human-style list with the Dusknoir engine. Twelve cards moved by Aug 11; on Aug 17 a Night Stretcher became the third Boss's Orders.
Change
Removed
Added
Dusknoir engine
−2 Duskull, −2 Dusclops, −2 Dusknoir
Measured out: the list without it won 64.7% head-to-head (N = 150).
Our forecast from the coaching canon, written before the run, was −5 to −10; the sign was wrong.
Poké Pad
−4 Poké Pad
82% of the 105 top-band teams run it. Adding one back measured −1.58pt
(95% CI −3.45 to +0.29) with the pilot byte-identical.
Supporter trim
−1 Carmine, −1 Judge
Part of the mono-Water rebuild; measured as a bundle, not per card.
Mono-Water core
+3 Basic Water, +1 Mega Starmie ex, +1 Pokégear 3.0
Energy for the one-energy 120 + 50 plan, a fourth copy of the only attacker.
Recovery and switch
+3 Night Stretcher (−1 on Aug 17), +2 Surfing Beach
Bring the attacker back; Surfing Beach is the deck's only switch.
Boss's Orders 0 → 2 → 3
The third copy measured −1.53pt (95% CI −2.76 to −0.30) with the old pilot.
Re-added with the targeting rules of Fig. 1; the bundle measured −3.29pt after the deadline.
Net parent → final: −6 Dusknoir line, −4 Poké Pad, −1 Carmine, −1 Judge / +3 Water, +2 Night Stretcher, +1 Mega Starmie ex, +1 Pokégear 3.0, +2 Surfing Beach, +3 Boss's Orders.
Sources: deck.csv of the parent (Jul 14), aqua (Aug 11) and the submission (Aug 17); effect sizes on the calibrated out-of-family composite (Figs. 4–6), pilot byte-identical within each test.

Expert intuition is reliable only where the expert has had fast feedback from a regular environment (Kahneman & Klein 2009); no one had such feedback about an AI pilot, so every orthodoxy was measured.
